profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer @ Greenlight

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Collaborate in strategic planning with leadership to determine direction and scale of business.
- Manage and guide engineering team in technical design and decision-making.
- Continuation of responsibilities in line with previous role.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Manage and facilitate multiple concurrent projects as lead engineer.
- Review code quality to ensure standards maintained and requirements met.
- Work with product managers to support in product design, technical requirements and decision-making based on client specifications.
- Engage in all stages of project lifecycle such as discovery, feature development and maintenance.
- Communicate with clients to determine needs, manage project scope and timeline.
- Develop and maintain numerous web applications (React, Vue, Mobx, Redux), mobile applications (React Native), and backend systems (Python, Django, Celery, Redis, Docker).
- Set up E2E testing infrastructure (Playwright, Cypress) for frontend applications that run during continuous integration workflows to reduce bugs reported in production environments.
- Set up and configure automated pipelines for deploying frontend platforms across multiple hosting services.

projects.title: Theia
projects.description:
iOS Mobile application that walks a user through an vision acuity exam and provides an approximate prescription for corrective lenses.

We placed top ten at PennApps 2016, and won best health hack.

projects.title: BeaconBits
projects.description:
Beacon Bits is a tool for system administrators and other IT professionals.

My team submitted this project at MangoHacks 2016 and won the Best Use of Amazon Web Services prize.

A Beacon is a small, WiFi-enabled device that submits information about the network to a cloud-based service. Administrators can see the data from a website.

We used an Arduino UNO as our development beacon. We used the Johnny-Five framework to diagnose the network by measuring ping rates and upload and download speeds.

I worked with the Arduino, configured it to integrate with the backend that was in Ruby on Rails running on Amazon Web Services. This was my first time working with Javascript, NodeJS and a RESTful API.
